thread:
maria: Heads-up: noticed a steady memory creep on worker-12 w/ longctx traffic when using INT8 KV pages. BF16 looks fine.

aj: How steady? over what timeline?

maria: ~1.2GB over ~6 hours on a 48GB instance. pattern only with INT8 quant profile + default slab_gc thresholds. warm_count for many slots stays >200 so compaction never fires.

kevin: Do you have a flamegraph or pprof? can you dump the KV internals?

maria: yep, uploaded a short profile and repro steps. repro is simple: run synthetic longctx workload (seq len 12k) hitting the same slot distribution.

maria: Repro command:
```bash
# run n=4 clients, each stream 20s sequences repeatedly
./tools/longctx-repro --clients 4 --seq-len 12000 --model rdx-7b-int8 --kv-skip 0.01 --duration 6h > repro.log 2>&1 &
```

maria: pprof snapshot (top KV-related):
```text
18.3%  runtime/kvcache.SlotRead
12.1%  runtime/alloc.slab_compact
9.9%   runtime/quant.dequant_handoff
7.2%   runtime/kvpage.fill_from_disk
6.8%   runtime/io.page_write_async
```

perf-bot: perf-alert: worker-12 memory_growth detected (+1.1GB/hr) since 2634998000.

aj: Interesting that slab_compact is non-trivial. That suggests compaction path is running but not reclaiming due to fragmentation or warm_count heuristics. Did you check slot residency distribution?

maria: Attached quick histogram: most used slots have residency ~8-12, but ~30% of slots are in the 1-3 range but pinned by warm_count > threshold (false positives).

kevin: Could be int8 page layout causing small pages to avoid coalesce (alignment). INT8 compresses but increases slot count so fragmentation increases. Also kernel selection for copy ops might be slower, delaying async frees.

aj: Two hypotheses: (A) warm_count ramp-up policy too permissive under INT8 (keeps cold entries alive), or (B) compaction miss because coalescing requires contiguous free runs that don't exist due to page stripe pattern for int8 packing.

maria: I tried forcing compaction every 5min via debug knob, memory stabilizes but tail latency spikes during compaction windows. So tradeoff between reclaim and latency.

kevin: Can we try a precision-aware compaction policy: for int8 mode, lower warm_count threshold and prefer background async compaction with smaller batch sizes to avoid big latency spikes. Also try a page layout tweak to reduce stripe fragmentation.

aj: Agree. Also want to quantify accuracy delta if we switch some hot slots to BF16 fallback temporarily. Is there a way to mark high-recall slots to keep BF16?

maria: We have per-slot hit-rate + fidelity metric in traces. I can flag top 5% of slots by fidelity drop and keep them at BF16. but that reduces memory savings. Quick numbers from earlier test: full INT8 gives ~3.9x memory reduction vs FP16 but BLEU/QA-macro drops ~0.8% on our eval set. selective BF16 on top 5% reduces memory savings to ~3.2x but recovers ~0.6% of the accuracy drop.

perf-bot: regression-note: accuracy delta logged under run 2635001200.

kevin: That looks promising. Plan: implement two small changes and run 12h A/B: 1) int8 compaction policy tweak (warm_count -30%), async compaction batch caps at 4 pages; 2) BF16-hot-slot fallback for top 5% slots. Measure memory growth, tail-latency, and eval fidelity.

maria: I'll push a canary to worker-12 tomorrow 06:00 UTC. Adding a flamegraph capture cron to run every 30m for 12h.

aj: Also add a kernel selection trace: annotate whether memcpy path used AVX2 vs cuda-kcopy path, because we saw slow copy kernels previously adding queuing that blocks compaction.

maria: added. infra-bot, reserve worker-12 06:00-20:00 UTC for canary.

infra-bot: reservation created: worker-12 locked for canary 2635080000-2635136000 by maria.

kevin: If canary looks good, let's prod roll to a subset of prod (5%) and keep telemetry for 72h. If mem growth persists, fallback to BF16 conservative profile.

maria: Action items:
- maria: push compaction knob + BF16-hot-slot logic to canary branch and schedule canary (today).
- aj: add kernel-selection trace points and memory-growth dashboards.
- kevin: prepare rollback plan + perf runbook entries (latency vs reclaim knobs).

aj: ll take the dashboard work. ping me when canary is running so I can validate traces.

maria: will do. thanks :thumbsup:

kevin: nice investigative writeup. this is a good example of precision-vs-memory tradeoffs in the KV layer.
